subject: research/anytime-liquidity
professional: an online-learning / prediction-market researcher (the Chen-Vaughan / Abernethy-Frongillo line of work on cost-function market makers as no-regret learners); first checks: is the time-varying-b regret bound the right one, is AdaHedge implemented as de Rooij et al. 2014 specify, does b_T ln N really bound the maker's loss when b changes mid-stream, and what is new against the anytime-Hedge and liquidity-sensitive-LMSR literature

evidence.correctness: Every number I recomputed matched, from code I wrote without importing the subject (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/b2968675-933a-541b-8835-9a181e723712/scratchpad/anytime-liquidity/indep.py). E1: closed-form sum_t t^(-1/2) = 2 sqrt(T) + zeta(1/2) + 1/(2 sqrt T) - T^(-3/2)/24 (zeta(1/2) = -1.4603545, DLMF 25.6) gives fixed 10.73/33.93/107.30/339.31 and anytime 14.64/47.44/151.19/479.30, ratios 1.3643/1.3981/1.4091/1.4126, identical to results.txt:2-5. E2: an independent eta-form Hedge with the CBL eta = sqrt(8 ln N/T) and its own best-response adversary gives regret 22.78 (fixed) and 31.13 (sqrt), bound 45.60, as results.txt:8-9. E4: AdaHedge written from de Rooij, van Erven, Grunwald, Koolen (JMLR 2014) pseudocode with exact FTL (uniform over leaders) at eta = inf gives regret 95.95/18.15/5.12/1.75 and Delta 64.08/11.83/3.44/1.27 at gaps 0/0.05/0.2/0.6, identical to results.txt:17-20 (the subject approximates eta = inf by b = 1e-9; no visible effect). E3: true concatenated doubling regret is 35.87/74.68/152.36 vs the reported sum-of-epoch upper bound 36.87/75.68/153.36; true ratio to anytime 1.65/1.68/1.69 vs reported 1.70, and an adversary reacting to the doubling market itself gives the same 36.87/75.68/153.36. Analytic: c* = 1/(2 sqrt ln N) minimises the integral bound to sqrt(T ln N) (whitepaper.md:12 algebra re-derived); the exact-sum optimum c differs (0.3177 vs 0.3295 at T=100, N=10) but only moves the ratio 1.3643 -> 1.3634. Ran experiments: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` output is byte-identical to experiments/results.txt (0.9 s).
evidence.completeness: Claimed artefacts, each run: 12-test suite (pass), experiments/run.py reproduces results.txt byte-for-byte, experiments/figure.py regenerates regret_vs_gap.svg with no git diff, whitepaper tables match results.txt to the stated rounding, live page https://marisstella.app/research/anytime-liquidity/ returns 200 and shows the summary, figure and links (shows '12 tests'). The one thing named and not done is the b_max truncation, which whitepaper.md:27 says was not analysed. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: `cd research/anytime-liquidity && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 12 tests, OK, 0.13 s. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (bound 1/(8b) -> 1/(4b); AdaHedge b = Delta/lnN -> Delta/(2 lnN); c* 2 -> 1.8), 3 survived: the adversary attacking the lightest instead of heaviest half (model.py:125, which produces every E2/E3 number), the doubling epoch using b for horizon 2n (model.py:75), and Delta over-counted by 1.5x (model.py:104, which makes the headline 'R <= 2 Delta' test easier, not harder). The tests check only inequalities against bounds; no test pins run.py output to results.txt (test_figure checks the SVG against results.txt, not results.txt against the code), so the reported constants 1.70, 22.78, 31.13 are unguarded.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (131 lines), run.py, figure.py, both test files. model.py is small, pure, stdlib, docstrings state the bounds; softmax is shifted for stability. Defects: run.py:36-51 re-implements the adversary and the AdaHedge b rule inline instead of calling model.py (a change to run_adahedge would not reach the 'adaptive vs adversary' row), with dead variables L and bsched (run.py:37,39); `from .model import *` and star-imports in tests and run.py; test class named T. A reviewer would ask for an adversary_losses variant taking a stateful market, then accept.
evidence.claims: Backed: every number in README:12, whitepaper abstract and section 2-4 tables is in results.txt and reproduces; 'regret analysis only, not a full trader model' and the limitations list (whitepaper.md:29-30) are present; MIT stated. Not backed / overstated: README:9 and whitepaper.md:33 say '10 tests', there are 12 (the live page says 12). whitepaper.md:30 lists 'the exact sqrt 2 price of an unknown horizon ... with the optimal constant c*' as a contribution: that is the standard anytime-Hedge/FTRL calculation (Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi 2006 sec. 2.3; Orabona's online-learning notes), and the whitepaper cites no prior work at all beyond the sibling project market-routing; AdaHedge is named but de Rooij et al. 2014 is not cited. README:12 calls the bound ratio '1.36->1.41 measured' though it is a computed bound, and '1.70x worse ... against a reactive adversary' compares a sum-of-epoch upper bound (true ratio 1.65-1.69), disclosed only as whitepaper limitation (4).
evidence.fitness: A researcher could reuse the code (stdlib, deterministic, 1 s) and the AdaHedge-as-liquidity framing. But nearest prior work is not engaged: LMSR = Hedge (Chen & Vaughan, EC 2010; Abernethy, Chen & Vaughan, TEAC 2013), liquidity-varying LMSR (Othman, Pennock, Reeves & Sandholm's LS-LMSR, 2013; Abernethy, Frongillo, Li & Vaughan's volume-parameterized framework, EC 2014; Li & Vaughan on liquidity axioms 2013), anytime Hedge (Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi 2006; Auer, Cesa-Bianchi & Gentile 2002) and AdaHedge (de Rooij et al. 2014). Against that, the sqrt 2 and doubling constants are known and the new part is the reading 'AdaHedge's Delta is the maker's subsidy', which is a two-line remark. The market question that would make it publishable (whitepaper limitation 1, path dependence of a b_t schedule with traders) is left open, though my check below suggests the subsidy bound itself survives it. As a programme step it is sound; as a paper it is a note.
evidence.domain: Against the online-learning standard: the time-varying bound b_T ln N + sum 1/(8 b_t) is the FTRL/decreasing-rate Hedge bound (de Rooij et al. 2014 Lemma 1 with Hoeffding delta_t <= eta_t/8), applied correctly for nondecreasing b; AdaHedge's b_t = Delta_{t-1}/ln N and R <= 2 Delta_T match the paper. Against market-maker practice: I simulated an LMSR whose b_t is nondecreasing with traders mostly buying the winning outcome (400 random runs, {S}/maker.py) and the maker's loss max_i q_i - revenue stayed <= 0.854 b_T ln N, consistent with the derivation C_b(q) increasing in b with derivative H(p) <= ln N; so the 'subsidy b_T ln N' reading holds for any nondecreasing schedule and the whitepaper's limitation (1) is more cautious than needed. Departures: one adversary family, N <= 10, i.i.d. Bernoulli data, no small-loss or second-order variants (all stated).

verdict: Small, correct and reproducible, but thinner than it says. Every number I recomputed from independent code matched: the E1 bound ratios from a zeta(1/2) closed form, the E2 regrets from a separate Hedge, and the E4 AdaHedge regrets and Delta from de Rooij et al.'s pseudocode; run.py reproduces results.txt byte-for-byte and a trader simulation confirms the 'subsidy b_T ln N' reading for nondecreasing b. The doubling penalty is 1.65-1.69 true rather than the reported 1.70 (an upper bound, disclosed as a limitation). The gaps are research-level: the headline sqrt 2 result is the textbook anytime-Hedge constant presented as a contribution with no prior work cited, and the market question that would make it new (trader path dependence under a b_t schedule) is left open; 3 of 6 seeded mutants survive because tests check only bound inequalities, and the test count in README and whitepaper is stale. Does not meet the bar (verification 2, claims 2; median 3). Fixable in a session: cite the LMSR-as-Hedge and anytime/AdaHedge literature and rescope the contribution, pin results.txt in a test, fix the test count.
